name: Booking.com RecTour 2024 Reviews Challenge dataset
time_coverage: dated reviews, span not confirmed in this pass
sample_issues: Licence: README says 'published under the following non-commercial license' but links CC BY-SA 4.0 (which is not non-commercial) and the card tag is 'cc' - contradictory; treat as research/non-commercial use only and a human should decide before anything derived is quoted in the pitch. Sampling caveat: guest_country is anonymised (codes like 'Zuc'), the sample is 2023 only, reviews were filtered to 'informative' ones with >=3 topics and only tens of thousands of properties, so shares are not population estimates. Heads are the first N bytes of each file, not random samples. Files were re-saved via pandas (CRLF line endings on Windows). The job-card URL (ceur-ws.org challenge PDF) was not fetched; data URL is the Hugging Face repo.

name: Booking-dataset-sample (Bright Data / luminati-io)
sample_issues: No LICENSE file in the repo (tos_or_license_flag=true): this is Bright Data promotional content scraped from Booking.com, and redistribution/usage rights are unstated; a human must decide before using it in any deliverable. Row count is 1,000 not 1,001 (job card counted the header). Single snapshot, single stay window, three cities, no timestamps beyond the stay dates; children and tax_description columns are entirely empty. The larger 30.4K product is paid and was not touched. Booking-datasets.png (627 KB marketing image) deliberately not pulled.

name: Booking-com/multi-destination-trip-dataset
sample_issues: Licence CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0: non-commercial and no-derivatives; a competition pitch is arguably non-commercial but a human should confirm before quoting figures. Country and city identifiers are anonymised (fictional country names, integer city IDs) so no real geography or regional split can be recovered; no price, room type or accommodation type column, so no ADR or STR/hotel split. README lists a created_date column that is absent from the files (no lead-time measure). Heads are the first N bytes of files sorted by user_id, so booker_country shows only 5 values in the head; the ground_truth file was pulled in full. Sample is multi-city trips only (4+ reservations per trip), so LOS and cross-border shares are not representative of all Booking.com bookings.

name: tx-hotel-heatmap
time_coverage: Multiple historical quarterly/monthly Comptroller filing periods through ~2026 (exact start year not stated in README excerpt)
sample_issues: No LICENSE file in the repo (author's build output; Comptroller HOT data itself is public record). data/box/texas-hospitality.tsv is an STR/CoStar-style property export (columns 'Data Participation', chain scale, FEMA fields) whose redistribution terms are unknown -- owner name/phone/contact columns were dropped from the saved samples, and a human should decide before quoting the STR fields; that TSV also has a repeated header row inside it so a few rows parse misaligned. Room counts come from the Comptroller filing (1-room placeholder filings exist; author filters rooms<2 and RevPAR>$2000). Revenue is taxable room revenue, not total; hotels matched across periods by normalised address, so renamed/re-permitted properties break the series. 2026Q2 is partial (Apr+May). The Socrata datasets on data.texas.gov (ids vmy5-jctb, ifh4-9tpn, er34-v24h, qik7-ypfg, 9xry-ncut, hdzd-884n) are local-HOT city-level reporting and permits, not this property-grain series; the property-grain source is the Comptroller's form-driven HOT public data query, which was not run here.

name: OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker
time_coverage: 2020-01 to ~2023-06 for most series (repo itself last pushed 2026-09-12; unclear if data files still update)
sample_issues: Series stops 2024-06-16 (repo pushes since then touch other files); no data for the pitch's forecast window. No LICENSE file: README asks users to name the data provider (Affinity Solutions) and cite the Chetty et al. 2020 tracker paper; job card flags no-resale attribution terms; a human should confirm citation in the pitch. Values are index changes vs Jan 2020, not dollar levels, and are seasonally adjusted by OI's own method. County file sampled only as a byte-range head (Jan 2019 to 6 Apr 2020) and contains spend_all only; the 41 MB full file is needed for county-level work. 2018-12-31 to 2020-01-12 rows are all '.' placeholders.

name: BNPL_Merchant_Dataset
time_coverage: merchant directories current; SEC financial panel 2015-2026
sample_issues: NO licence file in the repo (gh api reports license null): redistribution rights undetermined, treat as view-only research data. Adoption dates are Wayback first-capture of provider DIRECTORY pages, so Affirm rows cluster at 2020-11-29 and Zip at 2021-09-21 or 2022-06-25; date_precision is 'unknown' and confidence 'UNKNOWN' for all 278 rows and adoption_date_best is empty for every row, so the adoption table is not usable as an event date without manual work. Airbnb appears only in the Zip directory (Klarna's Airbnb partnership since 2023 is not captured because Klarna's directory was scraped by product category pages). The merchant directories are a single point-in-time snapshot with no history. bnpl_scraper.py scrapes affirm.com/klarna.com/afterpay.com/zip.co/sezzle.com and was not run; a human should decide on ToS before re-running. The sparse clone stalls on the 3,033-file CDX cache; use raw curls. Panel data is SEC XBRL-derived and duplicates what we already hold for ABNB/BKNG/EXPE/MAR.

name: airbnb-occupancy-tax
sample_issues: No LICENSE file (all rights reserved by default; thesis data, cite the repo, do not redistribute). Repo dormant since 29 Apr 2020. Data are the author's own airbnb.com calendar scrapes - compute_reservations.py / compute_bookings_cutoff.py were NOT run (ToS call for a human); only the committed derived outputs were copied. Reservation-date panels lack a year column (must be inferred from README: Jul 2018 - Dec 2019 check-ins); README itself flags a TODO to reprocess all data with later cleaning rules, so the committed CSVs may predate the final filters. Small n (11 cities x 11 periods). openpyxl absent in venv, so control_cities.xlsx was inspected via raw XML only.

name: pixelcrash/Sync-Rentals-Calendar
sample_issues: No licence file (all rights reserved by default) - reuse of the code or the ics needs a human decision; the ics is a real host's (kuenstlerzimmer.at) calendar, so treat as personal data even though it is public. Data is a single listing, 13 events, 2019 only, and 9 of 13 events have malformed SUMMARY (a date string, not a channel) and duplicate/overlap the labelled events - not a usable time series. The tool was NOT run (needs private feed URLs). Last push Jan 2020, effectively abandoned.

name: alujjdnd/Airbnb-Mar-2022-2023
sample_issues: Job card mis-describes the dataset (says Buenos Aires only, 2011-2023, 9.48 GB CSV/Parquet); it is actually ~116 markets of Inside Airbnb reviews gz files. Licence on the HF card is MIT but the underlying data is Inside Airbnb (CC BY 4.0 with attribution to Inside Airbnb); the MIT tag is the uploader's, not the origin's, so cite Inside Airbnb. Two files (Beijing, Shanghai) are 75-byte empties. natural_compressed/ file names are mangled/duplicated (e.g. 'united states la new.csv.gz' = New Orleans, 'stockholm.csv.gz' duplicated); use raw_dl/ which keeps the original Inside Airbnb names and dump dates. No listings/calendar files, so no supply or price data. Files are git-LFS on HF; no auth needed. Only 2 MB gz heads sampled, so each head covers only ~70-75 listings (sorted by listing_id), not a random sample.
